title: Tries
subtitle: A trie shares common key prefixes so each traversed edge refines the set of possible completions.
variables: L = query/key length in Python Unicode code points; Lmax = maximum dictionary key length (0 for no nonempty keys); k = requested suggestion count; T = total dictionary input size, sum(len(word)+1) over supplied key occurrences (so empty and duplicate keys count); P = number of allocated prefix nodes (P ≤ T+1 for an ordinary character trie); A = alphabet size; N = number of supplied keys/values, including duplicates; M = text length; B = chosen integer bit width; Z = sum(len(word)+1) over returned strings (including one slot per empty result string); R*C = board cells. Dictionary-backed child transitions are expected O(1); whole-string hashing/comparison costs O(L) initially/worst-case and substring creation is not free. Complexity uses a bounded-word arithmetic model; Python arbitrary-sized integers and normalization have additional costs. Trie storage is O(P) dictionary entries/nodes, but Python per-node constants are substantial. Q = number of queries for offline XOR; d = node degree; D = min(Lmax,RC). Empty keys still take O(1) method work, so lookup/update costs are O(L+1). For zero-column boards, validating row headers still costs O(R). Auxiliary space includes explicit stacks/recursion and excludes separately stated output; operations that create stored nodes identify persistent growth. All templates are standard-library Python 3.10+, iterative at unbounded input depth. C = maximum lexicographic string comparison cost for sorting suggestions. Cached suggestion output is a new list of existing string references; copying text would add O(Z). Hash expectations are not adversarial guarantees: many colliding keys can make a lookup linear in table size. For empty strings an O(L) walk means O(1+L) including fixed call/root work. Python list append/pop may resize linearly on a single call; amortized bounds apply over sequences.

templateDetails.preconditions: String keys, code-point edges, case-sensitive, no normalization. insert mutates trie and is idempotent for duplicates; search/starts_with do not create nodes. Empty key allowed; starts_with("") always true as root-path semantics. No recursion or external input mutation.
templateDetails.observation: Terminal belongs to the endpoint, including the root for an empty key.

templateDetails.preconditions: String multiset: each insert adds one occurrence, erase removes exactly one and returns bool. Missing erase leaves state unchanged. Empty word and prefix supported; count_prefix("") is total occurrence count. Prunes unused branches, not shared prefixes; stored trie intentionally mutates, caller strings unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: An erase validates before decrementing and only prunes zero-pass suffix nodes.

templateDetails.preconditions: Builds a temporary trie from string iterable, returns bool. Dot in pattern means exactly one arbitrary code point; no literal-dot escape syntax or star support. Empty pattern matches iff empty word stored; duplicates irrelevant. None terminal cannot collide with character keys. For repeated queries retain the built trie rather than rebuilding. Input unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: A wildcard frontier may grow; single-path O(L) no longer applies.

templateDetails.preconditions: Returns each distinct stored string starting with prefix exactly once, in child insertion-order DFS (not guaranteed lexical). Empty prefix lists all, empty word may be included; no match returns []. Input string iterable unchanged. Mutable path plus iterator stack avoids quadratic prefix copying on a single deep chain; sort returned words if lexical output is needed and add sorting cost.
templateDetails.observation: One mutable path prevents quadratic prefix-copying on a deep unary branch.

templateDetails.preconditions: Nonempty case-sensitive string roots; empty root raises ValueError. Returns a new sentence with shortest root replacements. split()/join() intentionally normalizes whitespace to single spaces and treats punctuation as ordinary token characters; adapt tokenizer to preserve whitespace. Empty sentence→"". Inputs unchanged.
templateDetails.observation: The first terminal wins only for shortest-root replacement.

templateDetails.preconditions: Returns whether text is a concatenation of zero or more dictionary strings; empty text true. Empty dictionary words ignored since they do not advance segmentation. Duplicates harmless, no mutation, no recursion or substring hashing. Lmax is maximum nonempty dictionary key length (0 if none). This returns feasibility, not segmentations or a ≥2-word concatenation guarantee.
templateDetails.observation: Reachable text indices, not a greedy longest root, drive correct segmentation.

templateDetails.preconditions: Reusable sequence of nonnegative ints within positive bits width. Returns maximum XOR over distinct positions when at least two values exist; empty/singleton returns 0 by convention. Negative/out-of-width values or invalid width raise ValueError. Inputs unchanged; duplicate values allowed. Stated O(NB) assumes word-sized bit operations; very large Python integer shifts have additional bit complexity.
templateDetails.observation: A higher XOR bit outweighs all lower bits combined.

templateDetails.preconditions: Four-direction rectangular board, each cell exactly one Unicode code point, string dictionary. Returns distinct found words once in discovery order, not sorted; duplicate inputs suppressed by terminal metadata. Empty word accepted as an empty path even on an empty board; empty board otherwise returns []. Cell cannot repeat within a path; board and dictionary unchanged. Temporary trie terminal removal suppresses duplicate output but preserves descendant paths; traversal is iterative. Board scan/validation is paid even when every supplied word is empty. Output reuses existing word strings, so actual list storage is O(number of results); Z is a conservative text-inclusive bound. Terminal metadata temporarily retains original word strings; T accounts for this text when words arrive from a one-pass iterable. If dictionary text is excluded as pre-existing input, working references/nodes are O(P+min(Lmax,RC)) plus result references.
templateDetails.observation: Visited cells are local to the current path, and terminal clearing only suppresses output duplicates.

templateDetails.preconditions: nums iterable of unsigned ints fitting bits; query iterable (x, inclusive_limit), x fits bits, limit may be negative. Returns maximum x xor eligible value, or -1 if none, in original query order. Copies/sorts internally, no input mutation. Integer bit costs assume bounded machine words; signed values require another contract.
templateDetails.observation: Monotone limits permit one growing eligible trie.

templateDetails.preconditions: Static case-sensitive Unicode strings, distinct lexicographic suggestions and fixed k≥0. Empty prefix queries root cache and empty string is allowed. Returns up to k references in a new list, not copied strings; C=worst word comparison cost, T includes input keys. Build hashes words and stores their references. Cache list appends have amortized cost. No caller mutation; changing popularity, deletion or variable k requires index redesign.
templateDetails.observation: Sorted insertion makes the first k cached words already the correct static ranking.

templateDetails.preconditions: String keys and finite numeric values; insert overwrites existing value, not adds another occurrence. sum returns total values for keys with prefix; empty prefix includes every key, empty key supported, missing prefix returns 0. Zero/negative values are valid; nodes are not pruned on zero totals. Internal state mutates on insert, not sum. Values and hashing use stated arithmetic/string cost model.
templateDetails.observation: Overwrites propagate a delta, not the replacement value again.

templateDetails.preconditions: Case-sensitive Unicode string dictionary iterable and text; returns the longest stored key that prefixes text, None if none. A stored empty key can return the empty string, intentionally distinct from None. Duplicates irrelevant, inputs unchanged. Repeated queries should retain the trie; then query is O(L) expected plus returned slicing allocation. Plain stored-string prefix lookup is not full IP routing; bit-address routing requires a binary-address model.
templateDetails.observation: Remember the last terminal before mismatch; deepest path existence without terminal is not a stored match.

practiceDetails.insight: Exact/prefix API. search is not startsWith.
Counts and erase. Count occurrences and update root pass count.

Foundation — Each dot branches one level; consume the entire pattern and check terminal. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: A dot consumes exactly one character.
Shortest terminal prefix. Shortest root wins; choose tokenization policy.
Cached top-three or prefix ranges. Deduplicate products if API requires unique suggestions.
Prefix aggregate delta updates. Overwriting a value requires adding delta, not full new value.
Trie-guided reachable-prefix DP. Greedy longest match can fail.
Trie + memoized enumeration. Materialized suffix strings can dominate space.

Transfer — A dictionary word itself is a trivial one-part split; require at least two nonempty pieces. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Do not accept the word itself as its only segment.

Transfer — Only descend through terminal prefixes when constructing a buildable word. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Every successive prefix must itself be a word.

Transfer — A greedy opposite bit at the highest available position dominates all lower choices. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Width must include every input bit.

Stretch — Sort queries by their upper bound and grow an eligible binary trie once. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Return -1 when no eligible value exists.
Trie-pruned board backtracking. No cell reuse; duplicate word output suppression.

Stretch — Every word contributes one pass through each prefix; sum those stored occurrence counts on its path. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Sum pass counts on nonempty prefixes; duplicates contribute.

Stretch — A reverse trie can match suffix/prefix alignments, but leftover segments must be palindromes. This is a stretch extension, not the basic trie template. Mastery: implement from a blank editor, explain the governing invariant and stated complexity, and demonstrate this check: Empty words, duplicate words, and ordered index pairs require explicit handling.

decisionProcess: 0–25 seconds — Ask what text means: lowercase ASCII or Unicode code points, normalization/case, empty keys, distinct versus duplicate insertions, ordering and mutation. Exact membership only usually favors a set.

25–55 seconds — Prefix path queries suggest a basic trie; whole words require terminals. Multiplicity/erase suggests pass+end counts; value overwrites/prefix sums need delta aggregates, not occurrence counts.

55–85 seconds — Identify branching/output: dot wildcard carries a frontier; completions traverse a subtree; fixed small-k static lexicographic suggestions can be cached; dynamic popularity cannot reuse that static proof.

85–115 seconds — Match composition: shortest root stops at first terminal; longest prefix remembers the last; segmentation needs reachable-boundary DP; board words need trie-guided path-local backtracking.
115–145 seconds — Numeric XOR means a fixed-width binary trie. Filtered XOR can sort by limit offline; signed/overflow semantics or online removals change the contract. State a high-bit greedy proof.

145–180 seconds — Budget O(P) Python node/dict memory, wildcard branches, output characters, sorting comparisons and hashing. Choose iterative depth handling; test app/apple, empty/duplicate/missing erase, Unicode, wildcard length, and a long chain.
